Batch 105 Forensic Discoveries: Crossing the 2,000 Milestone

Batch 105 officially crosses the landmark threshold of 2,000 verified and dated mystery radio broadcasts in the canonical archive (now 2,011 total). This batch dates 12 culturally foundational historical broadcasts across Hollywood comedy, country music origins, pre-WWII geopolitical speeches, vaudeville catchphrases, and literary masterworks: Bob Hope and Lucille Ball co-starring in Damon Runyon's racetrack comedy Sorrowful Jones on Screen Directors Playhouse (1949), 3 rare Mexican border blaster transcriptions from the original Carter Family (A.P., Sara, and Mother Maybelle Carter) broadcasting from XERA in Villa Acuña (1939), Patsy Montana performing her historic million-selling smash 'I Want to Be a Cowboy's Sweetheart' (1936), Charles Lindbergh's infamous pre-WWII America First address opposing U.S. intervention in European wars (April 1941), Jack Pearl's comedy sensation Baron Munchausen delivering his immortal line 'Vas you dere, Sharlie?' (1933), the Great Dane of comedy Victor Borge combining wit and piano virtuosity (1945), screen starlet Ann Blyth hosting the military hospital tribute Purple Heart Album with Tex Beneke (1947), Oscar winner Charles Laughton reading Dickens' The Pickwick Papers for Christmas (1944), and 'Magic Fingers' pianist Eddy Duchin playing 'Shine On, Harvest Moon' (1938).
